summary: Step 2 discovers what the raw reads (FASTQ) themselves carry in the 404 target genes, without ever touching the vendor's own variant caller — a check on whether the delivered callset (VCF) is trustworthy or whether it silently dropped something. A k-mer bait (a filter that keeps only reads sharing a short DNA substring with the target genes) swept 1,071,835,104 reads and matched 14,657,560 (1.368%, against a bait covering 1.361% of the genome — the two numbers agreeing is the check that the bait engine is correct). The recovered reads were aligned, called with two callers built on different statistical models than the vendor's, checked for structural variants (SVs, large deletions/duplications/inversions) and read-backed phased. Of six pre-registered claims, four were supported and two refuted; two more (H017, H018) were superseded outright because the named tools have no arm64 build and were swapped for equivalent-class substitutes. The step was first declared done with four planned stages unrun and the iteration's own blind gate red; a completion audit caught this, the missing stages were run, and one of them (annotating 1,199 alleles the vendor callset never reported) flipped H020 from supported to refuted.
why: A compound-heterozygous diagnosis (two different broken copies of the same gene, one from each parent) can only be trusted as far as the callset it's read from. If the vendor's caller silently missed an allele — because of a coverage gap, a caller-specific blind spot, or a filtering choice — no amount of downstream ranking recovers it; the analysis would be reasoning brilliantly from an incomplete record. Rebuilding the calls independently from raw reads, with a caller of a different statistical model, is the only way to check that. Skipping this step would mean trusting a single vendor pipeline with no cross-check at all, and — as the audit found — even running it under a scoring query that silently joined against the vendor's own annotation table would have quietly reintroduced exactly the blind spot it was built to catch.
verdict: H016 (a target gene carries a biallelic candidate) supported: ten do, three core-tier. H019 (phasing either closes the chain or names the gap) supported: it named the gap — none of 6,823 phase blocks reach BUB1B's coding span. H021 (bait recovers ≥ 90% of reads carrying a known allele) supported at 0.9052. H022 (≥ 99% concordance with the delivered callset) supported at 0.9957/0.9927 for SNVs. H020 (decoys yield fewer biallelic candidates per gene than targets) is refuted — after annotating the 1,199 alleles only the read-derived callers saw, targets and decoys tie exactly at 10/396; the earlier apparent 2x target advantage was a scoring artefact of joining against vendor-only annotation. H023 (no two-method-class deletion overlaps an exon of a rare-allele gene) refuted: one does, in a decoy gene. H017 and H018 are superseded, not resolved — they named specific tools (DeepVariant; Manta/LUMPY/GRIDSS) with no arm64 build, replaced by freebayes+bcftools and delly+dysgu respectively, and the underlying claims (≥99% concordance; two independent method classes) are re-tested as H022/H023 against the substitutes.

inherits.what: The 404-row tiered target set and 396-row decoy set fix what to bait and how much padding to add around each gene (core/mechanism-term ±50kb, net/decoy ±2kb). Step 2 also inherits step 1's caveat as a hard constraint on interpretation: because the target set is an enrichment (measured recall ≈ 0.335–0.36) and not coverage, an absence of a biallelic candidate in this step's target genes cannot be read as ruling out the true gene — only step 4's genome-wide scan can do that.

hands_to.what: The read-derived callset, its concordance with the vendor's, the SV consensus calls, and the exon-level depth/phase evidence all become inputs to step 3's alignment-free genotyping and copy-number work, which needs to know where step 2's short-read instrument ran out of reach (the paralogue-rich net-tier genes with sub-10x exons, and the unphased stretch inside BUB1B) so it can attempt those with a different method.

figures.name: recovery-funnel.png
figures.reads: Horizontal log-scale bar funnel: reads in the store (1,071,835,104) → reads sharing a bait k-mer (14,657,560, 1.3675%) → distinct fragments (7,886,613) → complete pairs after recovery, with a yellow dashed line marking the number of reads predicted before the pass ran.
figures.means: The 1.3675% matched fraction lines up with the bait's 1.361% genome coverage, which is the engineering check that the k-mer sweep is behaving correctly rather than over- or under-matching; every recovered fragment being complete (paired) confirms the FASTQ recovery step lost no mates.

figures.name: bait-uniqueness.png
figures.reads: Horizontal bars: the bait's off-target rate (repeated k-mers / total bait k-mers, 8.79%) plus zone- and k-value-sweep comparisons, colour-coded red (above gate) or green (below), against a yellow dashed 5% gate line.
figures.means: The off-target gate fails at 8.79% against a 5% target, and entry 086 shows no parameter reaches it — removing the wide padding entirely only moves the number from 8.79% to 8.38%, so padding is not the lever and cannot be dropped without losing the only reach the bait has for exon-scale deletions. This is a disclosed, unresolved gate failure, not a hidden one.

figures.name: bait-density.png
figures.reads: Box plots of surviving unique k-mers per base, one box per tier (core, mechanism-term, net, decoy), with a red dashed line at half the median density marking the reachability threshold and the count of genes below it.
figures.means: What the failed off-target gate was actually a proxy for: whether each gene is reachable at all by the bait. None of the sparse (unreachable) genes are core or mechanism-term — the genes step 2 actually draws conclusions from are all reachable; sparse genes are segmental-duplication families concentrated in the decoy set (16 of 21 sparse genes are decoys), which is why H020 is reported both over all genes and restricted to reachable ones.

figures.name: exon-coverage.png
figures.reads: A gene x exon heatmap for core and mechanism-term genes, one row per gene (ordered by that gene's thinnest exon), one column per coding exon ordinal, colour = mean depth (red below 10x, yellow at 10x, blue above, capped at 80x).
figures.means: 6,693 coding exons measured, median depth 44.96x, but 68 exons sit below the 10x floor where 'no second allele here' is a data gap, not a finding about the child. A per-gene average would hide every one of these thin exons; the grid does not. A further 61 sub-10x exons live in four net-tier paralogue-rich genes (NEB, GTF2I, GTF2IRD2, ANAPC1) where the uniqueness filter removed the bait entirely.

figures.name: phase-bub1b.svg
figures.reads: A three-lane rule diagram for BUB1B, offsets in base pairs from the baited window's own start (never a genomic position): coding exons (green), heterozygous sites the two callers agreed on (purple ticks), and read-backed phase blocks (blue) with unphased stretches inside the coding span shown red.
figures.means: Direct visual evidence for H019's verdict: none of the 6,823 genome-wide phase blocks reach BUB1B's coding span, and the widest unphased stretch inside the gene is named on the figure — meaning short-read fragments cannot say whether BUB1B's two heterozygous alleles sit on the same copy or opposite copies. This is a limit of the short-read instrument, not evidence either way about phase, and step 6 has to carry that distinction forward.

figures.name: index.html
figures.reads: Interactive contact sheet of the instrument-side figures: recovery-funnel, bait-uniqueness, bait-density, exon-coverage, and the BUB1B phase diagram.
figures.means: Same evidence as the five figures above, with hover tooltips for exact per-bar and per-cell values.

figures.name: caller-concordance.png
figures.reads: Horizontal bars, one per read-derived caller, showing agreement rate with the delivered (vendor) callset at co-called single-base-substitution sites, against a yellow dashed line at the pre-registered 0.99 threshold.
figures.means: Evidence for H022: both callers clear 0.99 (0.9957 and 0.9927), which is the check that licenses trusting the rest of step 2's read-derived calls. Indels are explicitly excluded because the delivered callset is unnormalised, so this concordance figure says nothing about indel agreement — the allele class the aligner is weakest at.

figures.name: filter-not-genelist.png
figures.reads: Grouped bars per tier (core, mechanism-term, net, decoy): share of genes with a biallelic candidate under 'any two variants' (red) versus 'rare and protein-altering' (green) filtering, same genes and same reads in both bars.
figures.means: The finding that outranks H020's own verdict: an unfiltered rule makes decoys win (nearly all decoy genes carry some two-variant pair, because everyone carries ~2 differences per gene — that describes a genome, not a patient), while the rare-and-protein-altering filter is what actually separates core genes from decoys. The filter, not the gene list, is what discriminates.

figures.name: sv-artefacts.png
figures.reads: Grouped bars by SV type (DEL, DUP, INV), each split into three categories by count: credible (span mostly baited, away from an edge, green), at a bait edge (yellow), and spanning unbaited gaps the bait itself created (red).
figures.means: Shows the bait's own geometry inventing false structural variants: the first unfiltered consensus run reported a 13 Mb deletion and a 40 Mb inversion in a living child, both artefacts of read-pair callers reporting the unbaited gaps between islands of coverage as one giant event. Requiring over half a call's span to be baited territory removes them, leaving credible deletions with a median length of 302 bp — the basis for H023's refutation (one credible two-method-class deletion overlaps a coding exon, in a decoy gene).

figures.name: results.html
figures.reads: Interactive contact sheet of the results-side figures: caller-concordance, filter-not-genelist, and sv-artefacts.
figures.means: Same evidence as those three figures, with hover tooltips for exact per-bar values and the H020 Fisher-exact p-values shown as notes.
